title: Deterministic purge orchestrator and retention evidence simulator
creator: Priya Sharma
description:
Problem: Customers require deterministic, auditable deletion of prompts/responses/request logs/metrics across regions and tenants while preserving compact, verifiable evidence bundles for auditors. Current retention work is fragmented: policy evaluation happens in multiple places, purge ordering is non-deterministic under concurrent migrations, and evidence exports are large and slow to generate.

Goal: Build a unified purge orchestrator that deterministically orders deletions, validates removals, and emits hypercompressed, signed evidence snapshots. Ship a retention evidence simulator that can run customer-specified scenarios (mix of TTLs, legal-hold flags, region constraints) and produce an audit report showing the exact sequence of actions, time-to-delete metrics, and resulting evidence bundles.

Scope: Implement orchestrator service, simulator CLI and UI integration, compact snapshot format (delta-encoded + zstd + HMAC), verification hooks to KMS/HSM for signatures, and integration with existing archival/export pipeline. Ensure compatibility with Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Out of scope: Full UI polish for Console dashboards (low-fidelity dashboards OK for rollout), reworking existing retention policy language DSL (we will read and interpret current policies), and long-term cold-archival storage changes.

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Deterministic+Purge+Orchestrator, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5123, retention-runner demo branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/retention-runner/tree/eng-22456
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator applies TTL and legal hold rules deterministically across tenants and regions; 2) Purge sequence reproducible given same inputs and ordered by policy precedence; 3) Evidence simulator can run historical scenarios and produce compact signed snapshots under 10% of raw export size for representative workloads; 4) Deletion audit logs contain checksums and signature references to KMS; 5) Integration tests validate that deleted records are irrecoverable from active replicas and that archived snapshots contain only allowed artifacts.
architecture_notes:
- Single brain orchestrator that consumes normalized retention-decisions stream (from policy-evaluator) and emits ordered delete intents to worker pools.
- Deterministic ordering: stable sort by (tenant_id, route_id, policy_priority, create_time, record_id) and deterministic sharding key for parallel workers.
- Evidence snapshot format: delta-encoding of record metadata + zstd level 9 + HMAC-SHA256 + KMS-signed manifest.
- Workers perform pre-delete verification: tombstone set, checksum after delete, and append verification entry to immutable audit ledger.
- Trade-offs: centralized ordering simplifies proofs but adds single-brain risk; mitigations: leader election + read-replica for dry-run and failover.
- For Private deployments, orchestrator runs as optional single-tenant controller with the same APIs but local KMS integration.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy in staging with simulator enabled; 2) Run simulator against 30-day production replay (read-only) to validate ordering and snapshot compression; 3) Canary delete on synthetic tenant in prod (low-traffic) under daily k-sweep; 4) Gradual ramp to small subset of customers (opt-in) and gather audit verification metrics; 5) Full rollout following compliance sign-off. Rollback via disabling orchestrator and falling back to existing best-effort purge pipeline.
metrics:
- Time-to-delete P50/P95 (target: P95 < 2h for standard TTLs under 99th percentile QPS),
- Snapshot compression ratio (target: >= 8x),
- Evidence generation latency (target: < 15 min for a 30-day tenant export),
- Verification success rate (target: 100% for canary runs),
- False-delete incidents (target: 0).
